_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL); indication based on overall response rate, with clinical benefit such as improvement in PFS or OS not demonstrated

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm, non-randomized, international, multicenter registration-directed study of pralatrexate with vitamin B12 and folic acid supplementation
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed or refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (complete response, complete response unconfirmed, and partial response) by International Workshop Criteria (IWC) per independent central review
pivotal_trials.n: 115 patients enrolled; 111 treated (safety); 109 evaluable for efficacy
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 27% (n=29; 95% CI 19, 36) in 109 evaluable patients, with CR/CRu 8% (n=9) and PR 18% (n=20); median duration of response 287 days. Responses lasting >=14 weeks occurred in 12% (95% CI 7, 20).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were mucositis (70%), thrombocytopenia (41%), nausea (40%), and fatigue (36%); most common grade 3/4 toxicities were thrombocytopenia (grade 4 19%), mucositis, and neutropenia (grade 3 13%, grade 4 7%)
target_moa: Folate analogue metabolic inhibitor; structural analogue of methotrexate taken up via the reduced folate carrier (RFC-1) and polyglutamylated by folylpolyglutamyl synthetase (FPGS), with dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) as its main target

advisory_committee.vote: ODAC met September 2, 2009 and voted 10 to 4 in favor of accelerated approval of pralatrexate

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (27%, with 12% of responses lasting >=14 weeks) from a single-arm trial, considered likely to predict clinical benefit

citations.quote: Although the trial supporting this application was a single arm, non-randomized trial, the magnitude of pralatrexate treatment, i.e., 27% response rate with 12% of responses lasting 14 weeks or more, most likely predicts clinical benefit in patients with PTCL.

confirmatory_requirement.text: At least two adequate and well-controlled trials to confirm clinical benefit, including a randomized maintenance trial in PTCL (1547-1) and a randomized trial in CTCL (1547-2)

citations.quote: Products approved under the accelerated approval regulations, 21 CFR 314.510, require further adequate and well-controlled trials to verify and describe clinical benefit. We remind you of the following post marketing requirements specified in your submission dated September 20, 2009. Submit clinical protocols for at least two trials to confirm the clinical benefit of treatment with FOLOTYN™ (pralatrexate injection). These requirements, along with any completion dates, are listed below.
1547-1 A randomized trial of maintenance treatment with pralatrexate in previously untreated patients with PTCL who have demonstrated a response to CHOP or a CHOP-like regimen.

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: FOLOTYN received orphan-drug designation (July 20, 2006) and fast track designation (September 28, 2006), was reviewed as a Priority application, and was granted accelerated approval on the basis of overall response rate from the single-arm PDX-008 trial, with two confirmatory post-marketing trials required to verify clinical benefit.
